chunks: He was asked about an animal slaughtered facing other than the Qibla. He said: 'There is no problem, as long as it was not done deliberately.'

And about a man who slaughters but forgets to say the name (Bismillah) — can his slaughter be eaten? He said: 'Yes, if he is not suspected (of bad faith), and if he was proficient in slaughtering before this, and he does not sever the spinal cord, and does not break the neck until the slaughtered animal is cold.'

key_terms.الذَّبِيحَة: dhabiha — the ritually slaughtered animal; the act or product of Islamic slaughter
key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: Qibla — the direction of the Ka'ba in Mecca, towards which Muslims orient themselves in prayer and ritual slaughter
key_terms.يَنْخَعُ: nakh' — the forbidden act of severing the spinal cord or medulla before the animal is dead, which renders the slaughter unlawful
key_terms.يُتَّهَمُ: ittiham — being suspected or accused of dishonesty or negligence; the Imam conditions the ruling on the slaughterer's trustworthiness
key_terms.يُسَمِّيَ: tasmiyah — the act of saying 'Bismillah' (In the name of God) at the moment of slaughter, a required element of halal slaughter

ai.seo_question: What happens if a Muslim forgets to say Bismillah when slaughtering an animal according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides rulings on two scenarios related to ritual slaughter: first, that slaughtering facing away from the Qibla is permissible if unintentional; second, that forgetting to say Bismillah does not invalidate the slaughter if the slaughterer is trustworthy and competent, provided proper slaughtering technique is observed. These rulings reflect the Shia jurisprudential principle that unintentional omissions do not nullify an act when the person is otherwise qualified and sincere.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the slaughtered animal slaughtered towards other than the Qiblah. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when it was not deliberate’.

And about the man who slaughtered, so he forgot to Name (Bismillah), can one eat his slaughter?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, when he was not accused, and was good at the slaughtering before that, and did not flip it over, and did not break the neck until the slaughtered animal was cold’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about an animal which is slaughtered facing a direction other than al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful if it is not intentional.’

He (the Imam) was asked about a man who forgets to mention the name of Allah; if it can be used for food. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it can be used for food if he is not accused of (unreliability), who before was able to slaughter properly, does not cutoff the spinal cord and does not break the neck until the animal slaughtered becomes cold.’”
